key_insight: Multimodal MoE models can accurately "see" image content but fail to "think" — i.e., they perceive visual signals yet routing mechanisms divert computation away from reasoning experts, producing worse reasoning than equivalent text-only inputs.
problem_solved: Explains and diagnoses why vision-language Mixture-of-Experts models succeed at perception but underperform on subsequent cross-modal reasoning, isolating routing distraction as a core failure mode.
method: Systematic behavioral and routing-analysis of multimodal MoE architectures to show cross-modal semantic sharing exists and to rule out simple alignment failures.
Identify and quantify "routing distraction": visual tokens disproportionately activate perception-oriented experts and reduce engagement of reasoning experts.
Propose targeted mitigation strategies (e.g., routing regularization, expert-conditioning or gating constraints) to rebalance expert utilization and restore reasoning performance.
impact: Clarifies a practical failure mode in large multimodal MoEs and provides actionable diagnostics and fixes, helping practitioners improve robustness and reasoning fidelity in vision–language systems.
visual_elements: Side-by-side bar chart: model accuracy on reasoning tasks for image+text vs text-only inputs (showing the gap).
Schematic of MoE routing: tokens routed to different experts with arrows highlighting "distracted" visual-token routing away from reasoning experts.
Heatmap/timeline of expert activation: contrast activations for visual vs textual inputs to illustrate under-engaged reasoning experts.
Before/after diagram: effect of a mitigation (e.g., routing regularization) showing restored routing balance and improved reasoning performance.
paper_title: Seeing but Not Thinking: Routing Distraction in Multimodal Mixture-of-Experts
paper_authors: Haolei Xu, Haiwen Hong, Hongxing Li, Rui Zhou, Yang Zhang
